name: go_missing_import_error
prompt:
Fix the Go missing import bug in parser.go.

The function NormalizeName uses strings.ToLower and strings.TrimSpace, but parser.go does not import the strings package, so it fails to compile. The fix is to add the strings import at the top of parser.go.

Requirements:
- Modify parser.go only.
- After the fix, NormalizeName must trim surrounding whitespace and lowercase the result.
- Do not modify main.go or go.mod.
- Do not create new files.

PATCH MECHANISM (IMPORTANT - read carefully, this overrides the default rule):
This case requires a file-level structural edit (adding a top-level import statement). It is NOT a function-body change. The default rule of using patch_candidate for single-file edits does NOT apply here.

- You MUST use patch_plan with exactly one replace_snippet op targeting parser.go.
- DO NOT use patch_candidate. Set patch_candidate to null. (Reason: adding a top-level import lives outside any function; patch_candidate is reserved for function-body changes and its literal-match safety policy will reject patches that span the package declaration.)
- The replace_snippet target_snippet must be copied verbatim from parser.go. The package declaration line is a good anchor.
- The patched_snippet must include the original anchor text unchanged plus a valid Go import declaration so that strings.ToLower and strings.TrimSpace compile.

Validation command: go run .
